MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 42 years
Gestational Age: 20 weeks (by ultrasound dating)
Indication for Testing: Advanced maternal age
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniocytes extracted from amniotic fluid. This test screens for the most common aneuploidies involving chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 using fluorescently labeled primers to amplify chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers. A minimum of four informative markers per chromosome were analyzed. Peak area ratios between 0.8-1.4 are considered normal (disomic), while ratios <0.65 or >1.8 indicate trisomy.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13:
Markers analyzed: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Result: NORMAL - Consistent with two copies of chromosome 13
Peak ratios: All within normal range (0.95-1.12)

Chromosome 18:
Markers analyzed: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386
Result: NORMAL - Consistent with two copies of chromosome 18
Peak ratios: All within normal range (0.89-1.08)

Chromosome 21:
Markers analyzed: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1437
Result: NORMAL - Consistent with two copies of chromosome 21
Peak ratios: All within normal range (0.91-1.15)

Fetal Sex: Female (XX)

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a normal chromosome complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) was detected in this fetal sample.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. It does not detect:
- Structural chromosome abnormalities
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Aneuploidies of other chromosomes
- Single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on these normal QF-PCR results, no further karyotyping is indicated for this sample. The residual risk for chromosomal abnormalities not detected by this test remains at the background population risk.

This test was developed and validated by [redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory.
